nodes.label: Board-Centric Architecture
nodes.rationale: The Board, not the User, is the primary ownership object. Designing around a User makes collaboration impossible later; scoping every entity to a Board lets multiple boards, members, invites, comments, attachments and activity be added without a future database redesign.

nodes.label: Profile Entity
nodes.rationale: One Profile per Auth User, kept separate from the auth table so application-level user data can grow independently of Supabase auth.

nodes.label: Board Entity
nodes.rationale: A Board represents a project (University, Internship, Startup, Personal) and owns its Members, Columns and Todos, so permissions have exactly one anchor.

nodes.label: Board Member Entity
nodes.rationale: Modelled as a many-to-many join so one user can belong to many Boards and one Board can have many Members — the shape team collaboration requires.

nodes.label: Board Invite Entity
nodes.rationale: Supports both email invitations and invite links; invites expire automatically so a leaked link is not a permanent access grant.

nodes.label: Column Entity
nodes.rationale: Columns define workflow stages and belong to Boards, NEVER directly to Users — user-owned columns would break sharing. They carry category, position and WIP limits.

nodes.label: Todo Entity
nodes.rationale: Todos reach a Board through a Column rather than owning a user reference, and are specified to eventually carry title, description, creator, assignee, priority, due date, labels, attachments, comments and activity history.

nodes.label: Board Ownership Scoping Rules
nodes.rationale: Board → Columns → Todos → Comments → Attachments → Activity: every level inherits scope from the Board above it, which avoids permission problems because authorization only ever has to resolve one ancestor.

nodes.label: Database Principles
nodes.rationale: Every entity carries id/created_at/updated_at and every mutable entity supports ownership, permissions and activity history; soft deletion is preferred over hard deletion so history and audit trails survive.

nodes.label: Board-Scoped Realtime Sync
nodes.rationale: Realtime synchronizes task create/delete/update, drag & drop, comments and member presence. Clients subscribe only to Board-specific events so a client never processes traffic for boards it cannot see.

nodes.label: RLS-Enforced Authorization
nodes.rationale: All authorization lives in Supabase Row Level Security; frontend authorization exists only for UI convenience. The database must stay secure even if the frontend is bypassed entirely.

nodes.label: Update Caches Instead of Invalidating
nodes.rationale: React Query stays the primary state layer; optimistic updates are preferred and realtime events patch existing caches rather than invalidating everything, because a full board refetch on every remote event defeats the point of realtime.

nodes.label: Future Scalability Requirement
nodes.rationale: Personal boards, shared boards, organizations and workspaces must all be reachable without redesigning existing tables — the reason ownership was pushed onto the Board up front.

nodes.label: Does This Belong To A Board?
nodes.rationale: The single test applied to every proposed feature. If it belongs to a Board, design it around the Board; never design around a User when collaboration is expected.
